source.title: Robust Learning Rate Selection for Stochastic Optimization via Splitting Diagnostic
source.authors: Matteo Sordello; Niccolò Dalmasso; Hangfeng He; Weijie Su

record.file_problem: none; supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimization methods and reports held-out test accuracy and overfitting for neural networks, bearing on V4's optimizer and generalization relationship through a new optimizer and experimental comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper tests SplitSGD, SGD, Adam, and FDR on neural-network tasks and reports test accuracy and overfitting. Rows below capture stated outcomes; numerical values are mostly in figures and are not reconstructed. Cited claims about SGD generalizing better than Adam are prior work, not study results.
record.test_reason: The CIFAR-10 experiments bear on V4: SplitSGD matches manually scheduled momentum SGD and outperforms Adam, indirectly placing scheduled SGD above Adam. Most other reported findings compare the proposed method with competitors without establishing Adam's performance relative to SGD.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that SplitSGD is robust to initial learning-rate choice, can outperform SGD, Adam, and FDR on certain architectures, and sometimes substantially reduces overfitting. They identify the additional parameter q as a limitation and demonstrate extension to SplitAdam.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a dynamic learning-rate schedule that splits training into two SGD threads for a stationarity diagnostic; neural-network experiments use momentum SGD and compare selected learning-rate ranges. It does not reproduce the optimizer-tuning protocol described in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Initial learning rate changes results; FDR's performance differs between η = 0.01 and η = 0.1 on CIFAR-10 ResNet. The authors report diagnostic-parameter sensitivity analyses for w and q, but no exact plotted values are transcribed.

fits_no_version.finding: SplitSGD improves held-out performance or reduces overfitting relative to several optimizers; SplitAdam improves on Adam for the LSTM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Splitting, averaging, and diagnostic learning-rate decay can improve generalization relative to their optimizer baselines.

record.peer_reviewed: Trans. Mach. Learn. Res. (venue stated in supplied metadata; paper body says under review as submission to TMLR)
record.problems: Most neural-network results are presented in figures without exact numerical values in the text. CIFAR-100 reports the two best runs per method. The comparison selects learning-rate ranges and does not use the limited-tuning protocol in V4. Authors acknowledge increased variability for SplitSGD in some settings.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying reported result omitted; figures with values not stated in the text are represented by the authors' explicit textual summaries rather than reconstructed numerical rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected architectural comparisons and learned local connectivity.

Equal or better training performance despite worse generalization; broader optimizer hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching Adam to SGD. The prose does not establish Adam versus SGD on Penn Treebank or the remaining image tasks.
Batch-size interventions and adaptations to large-batch training.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text lacks readable plotted comparator values. The V4 verdicts therefore rely on explicitly identified indirect comparisons in the prose. Failure to reproduce the original tuning protocol is not itself evidence limiting V4. The blanket limits_scope label across R1–R6 is unwarranted.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels are not tested.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures as a test of architectural bias; different architectures are evaluated on separate tasks.

Does not compare adaptive optimizers under the limited-tuning protocol described in the version; does not test switching Adam to SGD or decoupled weight decay. Reports Adam against SGD and other methods using selected learning-rate ranges.
Does not measure sharpness or compare generalization-gap measures.
Does not remove memorized examples or compare their removal with random-example removal.

rows.subject: CNN with two convolutional layers and a final linear layer
rows.size_stated: two convolutional layers; final linear layer
rows.operation_detail: Compared SplitSGD with SGD, FDR, and Adam on Fashion-MNIST; reports test accuracy over training.
rows.baseline: SGD, FDR, and Adam comparators; exact test-accuracy values are figure only
rows.value: Authors state that SGD, FDR, and Adam show clear signs of overfitting after reaching peak performance in the first 20 epochs; SplitSGD avoids this and reaches better overall performance, with peak performance better than any competitor.
rows.uncertainty: 90% confidence bands reported in Figure 12; omitted from Figure 6 for readability.
rows.locator: Section 4.2, Figure 6 (top left); Appendix D, Figure 12
rows.note: The stated outcome concerns the proposed SplitSGD versus Adam/SGD, not a general claim that adaptive optimizers often generalize worse under limited tuning.
rows.check: Shared overfitting and SplitSGD's superiority do not establish whether Adam generalizes worse than SGD. Split this proposed-method comparison from any readable Adam-versus-SGD result.

rows.subject: 18-layer ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared SplitSGD, SGD, FDR, Adam, and manually decayed SGD; reports test accuracy over training.

conditions.value: η = 1e−1, then decreased by a factor 10 at epoch 150 and 250

rows.baseline: SGD, Adam, FDR, and manually tuned SGD; exact values are figure only
rows.value: Authors state SplitSGD at initial learning rates 1e−2 and 1e−1 is better than both SGD and Adam; one setting achieves the same final test accuracy as manually tuned SGD in fewer epochs. FDR performs excellently at η = 0.01 and worse at η = 0.1.
rows.uncertainty: Average results of 5 runs; 90% confidence bands in Figure 12.
rows.locator: Section 4.2, Figure 6 (top right); Appendix D, Figure 12
rows.note: The comparison shows condition-dependent optimizer outcomes, including a learning-rate-dependent FDR result.
rows.check: Replace the bundled proposed-method comparison with scheduled momentum SGD versus Adam. The direction is inferred from SplitSGD matching scheduled SGD's final accuracy and outperforming Adam; exact comparator values are unavailable.

rows.subject: 18-layer ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared SplitSGD, SGD, and Adam; reports test accuracy over training.
rows.baseline: SGD and Adam; exact values are figure only
rows.value: Authors report two best runs per method; SplitSGD reaches higher peak accuracy than the other methods and stabilizes to higher test accuracy at the end for η = 0.1; diagnostic appears to work slightly better at η = 0.01.
rows.uncertainty: Two best runs per method; exact uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The text reports selected best runs rather than averages.
rows.check: SplitSGD outperforming both competitors does not establish their relative performance. The reported two best runs per method are a selected subset, and should not be treated as representative averages.

rows.subject: two-layer LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Compared SGD, SplitSGD, Adam, SplitAdam, and FDR; reports test performance and overfitting.
rows.measure: best and last test performance; overfitting
rows.baseline: SGD, Adam, FDR, and SplitAdam; exact values are figure only
rows.value: Authors state SplitSGD outperforms SGD and SplitAdam outperforms Adam on both best and last performance; FDR does not improve over standard SGD. Overfitting is described as very severe for SGD, Adam, and FDR, and very small for SplitAdam and SplitSGD.
rows.locator: Section 4.2, Figure 6 (bottom right); Appendix D, Figure 12
rows.note: The text states that FDR's result suggests its diagnostic does not work across a variety of scenarios.
rows.check: SplitSGD improving SGD and SplitAdam improving Adam do not establish Adam versus SGD. Severe overfitting in both baselines also cannot determine their relative held-out performance.

rows.subject: three-hidden-layer fully connected neural network
rows.operation_detail: Compared SplitSGD, SGD, and Adam; reports test accuracy over training.
rows.baseline: SGD and Adam; exact values are figure only
rows.value: Authors state most methods achieve very good accuracy, while SplitSGD reaches the overall best test accuracy at η = 1e−1 and great accuracy with small oscillations at η = 3e−2.
rows.uncertainty: 90% confidence bands in Figure 12; exact uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: This is a supplementary architecture/task outcome, not an adaptive-optimizer-only comparison.
rows.check: The best SplitSGD accuracy does not establish Adam's performance relative to SGD. Figure 12 contains confidence bands for Figure 6's experiments, not this supplementary FNN experiment.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Compared SplitSGD, SGD, and Adam; reports test accuracy over training.

conditions.value: SplitSGD: 1e−1 and 1e−2; other rates not stated

rows.baseline: manually tuned SGD, SGD, and Adam; exact values are figure only
rows.value: Authors state SplitSGD at both learning rates achieves the same test accuracy as manually tuned SGD in fewer epochs and beats SGD and Adam.
rows.uncertainty: 90% confidence bands in Figure 12; exact uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The text does not give numerical values.
rows.check: Replace the bundled proposed-method comparison with manually scheduled momentum SGD versus Adam. Its direction follows indirectly from SplitSGD matching scheduled SGD and beating Adam. Figure 12 does not provide uncertainty for this VGG19 experiment.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, manually scheduled momentum SGD versus Adam with searched initial learning rates
relationships.reason: R2: the text places SplitSGD above Adam and at scheduled SGD's final accuracy, indirectly supporting better held-out performance for scheduled SGD; exact differences are unavailable.
relationships.display_finding: SplitSGD reportedly matched scheduled SGD while exceeding Adam, but exact differences were unavailable and the indirect comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: VGG19 on CIFAR-10, manually scheduled momentum SGD versus Adam
relationships.reason: R6: the text reports SplitSGD matching scheduled SGD while beating Adam, indirectly supporting the SGD advantage; comparator tuning details and exact differences are unavailable.
relationships.display_finding: SplitSGD reportedly matched scheduled SGD while exceeding Adam, but exact differences and comparator tuning details were unavailable and the indirect comparison remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CNN on Fashion-MNIST; 18-layer ResNet on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; LSTM on Penn Treebank; FNN and VGG19 supplementary results
reader_labels.reason: The selected comparisons often favor SplitSGD over Adam, but outcomes depend on model, dataset, learning rate, and reporting subset; these experiments do not establish the version's limited-tuning claim. Rows R1–R6.
